title: Review-qualified goal closure
description: Objective: close J1's remaining evidence-authority gap: goal.close currently trusts opaque caller-supplied verification/review witness refs. Deliverable: a daemon prerequisite composer that reads the exact durable EvidenceReceipt and ReviewOutputAccepted records for the candidate/result, binds their hashes and zero-authority proof into the core closure witness, and only then invokes the existing goal reducer/commit path. NOT in scope: new core rules, review-round persistence, verifier execution, UI, or canary tests. Depends on Durable verification receipt dispatch and the landed review persistence task task-9011e3b32c414e9ca0d49f49fdfaaf08. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-services.ts, goal-services.test.ts, a focused goal-qualification.ts module, and apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts refusal vocabulary if required. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: goal.close derives its verification, review, result, and zero-authority witnesses from matching durable production records; request payload refs/truth labels alone cannot satisfy closure.

Missing receipt, non-passing/UNKNOWN receipt, mismatched result hash, absent ReviewOutputAccepted, stale review package, or remaining authority each refuse with a distinct stable daemon-prerequisite code/layer and commit nothing.
A fully matching verified/reviewed result closes the goal through the existing core reducer in the third J1 human action; no extra human command is introduced.
Replay is idempotent with one durable closure row, and earlier review/evidence records remain readable and byte-identical.
Focused daemon and repo typecheck gates exit 0; the worker mutation-drills the durable read rather than a request-field check.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: TDD, evidence half. Write `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-qualification.test.ts` RED against the not-yet-written `qualifyGoalClosure(store, projectId, goalId)`. One case per durable state, each pinning the EXACT code AND that the refusing layer is `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`, and each re-reading the store to assert the goal aggregate did not move and `decisionCount` did not grow: (1) approved node in scope with no `FoundationVerificationReceipted` row naming it -> RECEIPT_ABSENT; (2) two receipts whose `receipt.graphIdentity` is the same node -> RECEIPT_AMBIGUOUS; (3) a receipt whose durable bytes were tampered after the fact via `commitRaw`-style direct write so the re-encode byte-compare in `readStoredReceipt` fails -> RECEIPT_UNREADABLE; (4) a receipt read back with verdict FAILED -> NOT_PASSED; (5) the attempt record mutated after verification so `readFoundationAttemptRecord(store, row.attemptAggregateId).digest !== row.recordDigest` -> RESULT_DIGEST_MISMATCH. Cases 1-5 must be distinguishable from each other, not merely all-refused: assert the code, since a single earlier guard answering for all five would otherwise pass (see `mem:refusal-test-answered-by-earlier-guard`). If the arms are written as a swept table, assert the generated case count is 5 and > 0.
implementationPlan.note:
THIS IS THE STEP THE REJECTION LANDED ON. Arms 1-4 were already correct and are untouched. Arm 5 was the defect, and it is now two arms.

WHAT WAS WRONG (QA's measurement, reproduced): the RESULT_DIGEST_MISMATCH case seeded a SECOND RECORDED event on the dispatch aggregate, which makes `readFoundationAttemptRecord` answer AMBIGUOUS. `verifiedResultHolds` is `stored.ok && stored.digest === receipt.recordDigest`, so the `ok` clause refused and the digest comparison beside it was never evaluated. The enumerated DoD 2 arm "mismatched result hash" was therefore never exercised, and QA's mutant — replacing the whole expression with `stored.ok` — kept all 2170 daemon tests green. Global rail 1 exactly: an earlier layer answers first and the assertion detaches from its subject.

WHAT I DID, both arms kept because both durable states are real:
- The original case stays as the RECORD-UNREADABLE arm, retitled "when the verified result no longer reads back" and now ASSERTING its own precondition, `readFoundationAttemptRecord(...).ok === false`, so it can never again be mistaken for the digest arm.
- A new arm reaches the digest clause: `seedProvenAttempt` gives node-1 a real record and activation, a real PASSED receipt is seeded for the OUT-OF-SCOPE node-src purely as a template, and `plantReceipt` commits one canonical receipt naming node-1 with `recordDigest` set to "f"*64. It asserts `stored.ok === true` AND `stored.digest !== "f".repeat(64)` before acting, so the ok clause provably cannot answer and only the comparison can.

WHY PLANTING IS NECESSARY AND NOT A CHEAT: a receipt the real chain mints carries the record's own digest BY CONSTRUCTION, so this guard is unreachable from any honest seed — which is precisely why it was unguarded. The planted bytes still go through `encodeFoundationPayload`, so `readStoredReceipt`'s decode/re-encode byte compare accepts the row exactly as it accepts a real one; nothing is mocked and no production surface is bypassed.

ALSO ADDED HERE, closing QA's informational survivor (a): "indexes the stored row a receipt points at, never the bytes that pointed at it". A decoy row is committed to its OWN aggregate while its `verificationId` field names another verification, so the scanned bytes claim node-1 while the row they point at is the real out-of-scope node-src receipt. Reading the scanned value would admit evidence for a node nothing verified; reading the stored row leaves node-1 with none, so the answer is RECEIPT_ABSENT. This makes the module's headline claim — "THE SCANNED BYTES ARE NEVER THE ANSWER" — falsifiable for the first time. `commitRawReceipt` gained one optional target-aggregate parameter to express it.

DRILLED, not asserted: mutant `stored.ok && stored.digest === receipt.recordDigest` -> `stored.ok` now fails exactly "refuses RESULT_DIGEST_MISMATCH when the receipt claims a digest the record does not hold" (1 failed / 16 passed). Mutant `receiptFrom(stored.row)` -> `receiptFrom(scanned.value)` now fails exactly the decoy test (1 failed / 17 passed). Both reverted, both files sha256-verified back to their committed bytes.

POSITIVE ARM, and it is load-bearing because a refusal-only suite is blind to a wrong accepted value (`mem:refusal-only-suite-cannot-see-a-wrong-accepted-value`): a fully verified + accepted node yields `ok`, and the test RECOMPUTES the expected `acceptanceClosureRef`, `completionNodeAcceptedRef`, `obligationsHoldRef` and `zeroAuthorityProofRef` from the durable bytes it seeded and asserts equality field by field, plus `truthClass === "DAEMON_VERIFIED"` on both witnesses. implementationPlan.note:
THE OTHER TWO REJECTED ITEMS LIVE HERE. Arms 6, 8, the re-plan and later-round staleness arms, and the positive arm were all correct and are untouched. Two guard-pairs were unreachable and are now reached clause by clause.

DEFECT A — the review cross-check's two operands CO-VARIED. `stageAcceptance` hardcodes `reviewInputDigest: "b".repeat(64)` among its defaults, and the test overrode only `verifierReceiptId`/`verifierReceiptSha256`. So the staged acceptance disagreed with the real receipt on BOTH fields at once, and `if (verifier.receiptSha256 !== accepted.verifierReceiptSha256 || verifier.receipt.reviewInputDigest !== accepted.reviewInputDigest)` would refuse with EITHER clause deleted. The comment claiming "only the sha256 is wrong" was false. Now two cases, one clause each, each passing the REAL value through for the field it is not testing and asserting that precondition after staging: "when only the acceptance's receipt sha256 disagrees" and "when only the acceptance's review input digest disagrees".

DEFECT B — the zero-authority identity comparisons were never evaluated. The existing case blurs the activation history, which only makes `readsBackAs` null, so the `account.readsBackAs === null` clause answered and both identity comparisons deleted green despite the asserted message naming them. Three clauses share one message here, which is exactly what hid it. The blur case is KEPT as the null arm, with a comment stating it reaches only that clause, and two new cases reach the identity clauses with `readsBackAs` non-null: node-1 gets a real record and activation via `seedProvenAttempt`, a receipt is planted naming node-1 with the correct `recordDigest` and correct sibling identity but a wrong `leaseIdentity` (and its mirror with a wrong `effectIdentity`), and each asserts the live identity differs from the planted one before acting.

DRILLED, four mutants, each killed by exactly its intended test and each reverted with sha256 verification:
- delete the lease clause (goal-qualification.ts:159) -> fails only "refuses AUTHORITY_REMAINS when the activation reads back as a different lease" (1 failed / 16 passed)
- delete the effect clause (:160) -> fails only "...as a different effect" (1 failed / 16 passed)
- delete the receipt-sha256 clause (:113) -> fails only "when only the acceptance's receipt sha256 disagrees" (1 failed / 16 passed)
- delete the reviewInputDigest clause (:114) -> fails only "when only the acceptance's review input digest disagrees" (1 failed / 16 passed)
Before this retry, all four of those deletions left the suite fully green.

Note for QA on the accounting: the planted-receipt cases seed their template from an out-of-scope node (`node-src`), whose own activation carries `nodeKey: "node-src"` and is therefore skipped by `zeroAuthority`'s `byNode` lookup rather than interfering — the only account that reaches the identity clauses is node-1's own.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of the named cases:
- Concurrent second close: unchanged and still bounded by the goal's expected-version CAS; the module's header records honestly that read and write are not one transaction and that the residual exposure is a STALE derivation, not a forged one.
- Empty approved scope: `readApprovedNodeScope` null refuses REVIEW_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED; an empty node list would compose over an empty `bound`, which is why the positive arm asserts the refs recomputed from seeded bytes rather than merely `ok`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
TWO FORKS WERE PUT TO THE HUMAN IN THE REPL AND BOTH WERE DECIDED; do not re-open them.

FORK 1 - what happens to the payload witnesses. Considered (a) derive-and-replace and (b) declare-and-cross-check (the `expectedRecordDigest` / CANDIDATE_STALE pattern from foundation-verification-contracts.ts:146). HUMAN CHOSE (a): the composer derives both witnesses from durable bytes and hands THOSE to `reduceGoal`; the payload keys stay required at ingress for wire compatibility and are inert. (b) was rejected because it needs a seventh payload-mismatch code that DoD 2 does not enumerate, and because every fixture would have to compute derived hashes. The inert-field smell is answered by a test in both directions, not by a comment: garbage payload refs + real durable records -> CLOSES; perfect payload refs + no durable records -> REFUSES.

FORK 2 - what 'remaining authority' means. Design line 278 demands proof of zero live planning/execution/review/qualification leases, attempts, processes, effects, resources, provider slots, funding holds, fences and reconciliation items. NONE of those has a durable terminal record: the activation ledger writes `EffectActivationCommitted` plus exactly three transitions (GRANT_CONSUMED, PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED, PROCESS_OBSERVED) and no release event exists anywhere in apps/daemon, and `LeaseRecord.state` is frozen at ACTIVE by event immutability so it carries no liveness signal. Considered reporting blocked for a prerequisite that lands release records. HUMAN CHOSE the accounted-for-activations measure: every durable activation whose attempt record carries a `nodeKey` in the approved scope must be named by that node's PASSED evidence receipt (`leaseIdentity`, `effectIdentity`); anything unaccounted or unreadable refuses. It is an honest subset of design 278, measurable on committed bytes today, and it fails closed.

Also considered and rejected: a second frozen refusal vocabulary in the new module. The existing `GOAL_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES` in goal-close-prerequisite.ts is the right home and is already asserted by goal-services.test.ts:174, so it ratchets for free.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED ON COMMITTED BYTES, 2026-08-17. The Serena memory `task-task-8f9305b9bb5e4b8db327a55981b2ea0e-handoff` is OBSOLETE: its 'ZERO EvidenceReceipt' grep and 'apps/daemon/src/evidence/ DIRECTORY ABSENT' are both false now. Commands run and results:

- `grep -rn EvidenceReceipt --include=*.ts -l apps packages adapters` -> 12 files including apps/daemon/src/evidence/foundation-verification-{contracts,service,store}.ts (249/193/183 lines, each with a git-tracked .js bridge).
- READ PATH THAT EXISTS: `readStoredReceipt(store, verificationId)` in foundation-verification-store.ts:109 returns `{ok:true, authority:"PROVEN_RECEIPT", digest, row, verdict}` and is the ONLY byte-checked path (it re-decodes, RE-ENCODES and byte-compares against the stored payload at :91-105). Absent / ambiguous / unreadable are already three distinct answers there.
- The durable row body is `verificationReceiptBody` (contracts:202-218): attemptAggregateId, candidateRoot, receipt (the whole EvidenceReceipt), receiptSha256, recipeSha256, recordDigest, verdict, verificationId, plus capture bindings. `row.receipt.graphIdentity` IS the nodeKey (service.ts:158 sets `graphIdentity: String(loaded.record["nodeKey"])`), which is the only durable node->receipt edge and is what the index in step 5 keys on.
- REVIEW HALF: `readReviewLedger(store, projectId, subjectRef).accepted` (review-read-model.ts:140-148, 180) yields `AcceptanceRecord {policyDecision, reviewInputDigest, reviewerCalibrationDigest, verifierReceiptId, verifierReceiptSha256}`. `readVerifierReceipt(store, projectId, receiptId)` (verifier-receipt-ledger.ts:85) re-reads the VerifierReceiptV1 and returns `receiptSha256` - comparing it to the accepted value is the real 'stale review package' discriminator.
- NOTE THE TWO RECEIPT FAMILIES ARE DISJOINT. `AcceptanceRecord.verifierReceiptId` is a VerifierReceiptV1 (review's own, command kind `internal.integration.verifier_receipt`), NOT the foundation EvidenceReceipt. There is no shared hash between them, which is why 'mismatched result hash' is defined as `readFoundationAttemptRecord(store, row.attemptAggregateId).digest !== row.recordDigest` - the result moved after verification. That is a real durable comparison; do not invent a cross-family hash.
- CORE CONTRACT: `validClosure` (goal-validation.ts:159) demands exactly acceptanceClosureRef, completionNodeAcceptedRef, noCurrentPreparationGeneration===true, noPendingDraftOrSupersession===true, obligationsHoldRef, and truthClass in {DAEMON_VERIFIED, HUMAN_APPROVED}. `validZeroAuthority` (:167) demands exactly zeroAuthorityProofRef + that truthClass. `exact()` means EXTRA KEYS FAIL - the derived object must carry these keys and nothing else.
- LAYER: `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` is already in `SERVICE_REFUSED_BY` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:33-42) and `refuse()` there takes a plain `code: string`, so bootstrap-ledger.ts needs no edit. It is REMOVED from the owned paths the task description listed.
- STORE SURFACE: `store.readEventsByTypeAfter(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit)` exists (sqlite-event-store.ts:354) and is the scan used for both the receipt index and the activation sweep. The activation ledger record lives ON THE ATTEMPT AGGREGATE (`readFoundationActivationHistory(attemptAggregateId, eventsOf(store, attemptAggregateId), projectId)`, verification-service.ts:167), which is what makes the authority check precise rather than a whole-project sweep.
- CONSUMER-EDGE RAIL: `createFoundationVerificationService` has ZERO callers outside apps/daemon/src/evidence/ (grepped). This task is its first real consumer edge, which is exactly what the pure-package rail asks for.
- GATE LEGS RESOLVE: apps/daemon/package.json declares name `@moe/daemon` with `typecheck` and `test` scripts, so neither --filter leg is the silent exit-0 no-match case.
planningNotes.risks:
1. BIGGEST RISK - THE FIXTURE, NOT THE COMPOSER. Seeding one durable `FoundationVerificationReceipted` row needs the whole real chain: seedReadyProject -> activation ingress -> launcher authority -> recordProvenFoundationAttempt -> sealRecipe -> verify() spawning a REAL node child. Model it on apps/daemon/src/evidence/foundation-verification-service.test.ts:1-70; do not shortcut it with a recording launcher, because a receipt minted from a fake process is the mock-backed acceptance the rails forbid. Budget step 2 accordingly; if the chain will not seed, report blocked rather than narrowing the DoD.
2. `runVerifierProcess` keeps a MODULE-LEVEL run registry keyed by grantId (documented at foundation-verification-service.test.ts:66-68). Two seeded nodes sharing an effect intent share a grant and the second adopts the first one's run. Derive each seeded node's intent from its nodeRef.
3. The two harnesses both use PROJECT_ID "project-1" (bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:35 and recovery/restore-test-harness.ts:32) so they share one store - convenient, and also the reason a seeding call can collide with the goal aggregate version the close envelope hardcodes (`envelope("goal.close", 2, ...)`, bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:343). Verify the version rather than assuming the fixture writes only to other aggregates.
4. `completionNodeAcceptedRef` HAS NO DURABLE SOURCE. Grep finds `completionNode` only as a test literal at bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:269 and in the core type. Deriving it over the whole approved node set is the deliberate conservative choice; say so in a comment, and do not quietly pick scope[0] or the last element.
5. `exact()` in goal-validation.ts rejects EXTRA keys. A derived witness carrying a helpful debug field fails `validClosure` and the core refuses with a code that looks nothing like the real cause.
6. Mutation drills run in a SHARED worktree (`mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree`): a peer's task-completion hook can commit a whole tree and swallow the drill so git reads clean. Snapshot the file hash before each drill and restore by content, not by `git checkout`.
7. Vitest workers die on a held SQLite handle - every seeded store must go through the harness `closeStores` in `afterEach`.
8. A refusal test whose seeded condition is answered by an EARLIER guard passes while testing nothing. The five evidence arms in step 3 sit behind each other in one loop; assert the exact code per arm and, for the two REVIEW_PACKAGE_STALE guards sharing one code, make the seeded condition itself the discriminator.
9. Per-file cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE. goal-qualification.ts is the one at risk; the split into goal-qualification-reads.ts is pre-authorised in step 5 and both halves need a .js bridge.
